audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never names a Sylas ability — it is "his Q lash-explosion", "his W shield-slam", "his E chain-dash" throughout — and the one description it does give is wrong. early and wants.you[1] both call Kingslayer a "shield-slam".
audit.why: Riot's Kingslayer text: "Sylas lunges at an enemy with magical force dealing damage and healing himself against enemy champions." It is a lunge and a heal, with no shield anywhere in it, and the heal only applies against champions. That distinction is the whole reason Grievous Wounds is the right buy in this lane and the reason denying him the hit shuts the sustain off entirely — neither of which follows if you think it is a shield. The other names matter too: Chain Lash is 10s at 775 range with a delayed explosion at the intersection, Abscond is 13s at rank 1, Hijack is 80s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: All four abilities named across both layers, Kingslayer restated as a champion-only heal, and real cooldowns attached in spikes, wants, whys, breakdown.cooldowns and the do/don't descriptions.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer describes Abscond / Abduct as "His dash + stun (recast pull)" in tldr's tracked ability, dosFull[0], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]. It also describes the recast as pulling the enemy.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits." The recast pulls HIM to you, not you to him, and the kit file's flags for E are projectile and dash with no hardCC. The direction matters for a champion whose only escape plan is walking out of range: Abduct is how he re-closes the gap you just made, so disengaging into it is worse than standing still.
audit.corrected: Restated as a dash out plus a recast that pulls him back onto you, in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], dontsFull[0], report[5], spikes[1] and wants.foe[1]. I did not assert either way on a stun — see notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hijack's cooldown appears nowhere, and both layers advise "only commit your R when his is down" as though the two ultimates trade evenly.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30. Public Execution is 130/115/100. At every rank Sylas's ultimate is available roughly twice as often as the one he is stealing, and by rank 3 it is 30s against 100s. "Wait until his is down" is therefore advice that resolves against the reader most of the time, and the honest framing is that she will not usually get a clean window — she gets the window when she forces it, immediately after he spends Hijack on something else. Petricite Burst is also absent: every spell he casts arms an AoE bonus-damage attack and gives him attack speed, which is where his auto trades come from.
audit.corrected: The 80s-versus-130s comparison written into spikes[2], mid, tldr, whys[6], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Petricite Burst added to mid, whys[1] and phases[1].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and mid say Sylas answers with "your own blink-suppress armor-pen knockdown"; late says "your R passive heals you on every hit"; whys[5] says "your R passive tops you off".
audit.why: Public Execution has no armour penetration and no healing. It blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. Against Sylas the invented heal is especially costly, because the whole lane is a sustain race he wins — telling the reader they out-heal him is telling them to take the fight he is built for.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the crash stun, and with Grievous Wounds named as the actual answer to Kingslayer.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys[] array is off its stages. whys[1] sits under "Level 2" but opens "His Q-W drain still out-sustains your two-ability trades at 4-5"; whys[3] sits under "Levels 4-5" but describes the level-6 ultimate exchange. phases[1].why also repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield" error.
audit.why: A reader at level 2 is given advice about level 4-5, and a reader at 4-5 is told to use an ultimate they do not have. Both stages have real content: level 2 is where Petricite Burst's charge timing decides the auto exchange, and 4-5 is Ambessa's longest cooldowns against a Kingslayer that is down to 9s by rank 3.
audit.corrected: whys[1] and whys[3] rewritten onto their own stages; phases[1].why corrected.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart opens "Skill" while whys[0] says Sylas chips you while you have "no combo to answer", gives Ambessa levels 4-5 in neither layer consistently, and hands Ambessa the two-item stage while whys[6] says "He out-scales".
audit.why: At 50.23% over 1073 games this is as close to even as the dataset gets, but the shape is not flat. The packet levelChart is Sylas, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Skill, Ambessa, Sylas — his at level 1 before her combo exists, hers through the middle, his again once AP and cooldown reduction land.
audit.corrected: Level 1 flipped to Sylas in both layers, and phases[0].why rewritten to say why. The two-item stage should read "Sylas" and levels 4-5 "Ambessa", but "Ambessa" is 7 characters against "Sylas" 5 and "Skill" 5, so those cross the band. Documented in notes.

audit.why: Each has a concrete answer: Kingslayer only heals off champions, Abduct pulls him back the instant you disengage, Drakehound's Step needs a cast to fire, and Hijack hands your own ultimate back at you.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten against the kit.

Bait his E chain-dash first — once it's down he can't peel your dash.

notes:
UNVERIFIED, and the reason one audit item is Medium rather than High confidence: the full layer describes Abduct as a stun ("His dash + stun (recast pull)"). Riot's Data Dragon text for Abscond / Abduct says only "Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits", and champ-data/_kits/sylas.json flags E as projectile + dash with no hardCC. Description and flags agree there is no CC, so per the brief I trusted the description — but I did not write "it does not stun" anywhere either, because a Data Dragon summary omitting a CC component is a plausible failure mode and asserting the negative would be worse than saying nothing. The corrected strings describe the dash and the self-pull and leave the question open. Worth a wiki check before anyone writes it either way.

The Hijack cooldown comparison is the most useful addition. Both layers said "only commit your R when his is down" without ever noting that Hijack is 80/55/30 against Public Execution's 130/115/100 — his ultimate is up about twice as often at every rank, and 30s against 100s at rank 3. The advice as written resolves against the reader most of the time.

The packet defect line ("never names any of Sylas's abilities") was accurate, and the naming gap was concealing a real error: Kingslayer described as a "shield-slam" in two places when it is a champion-only heal. That distinction is what makes Grievous Wounds core here rather than optional, and _missing-interactions.json flags this pair for exactly that.

COULD NOT FIT IN THE BAND, for the user to apply by hand: content win[3] and full phases[3].side should read "Ambessa", and content win[6] and full phases[6].side should read "Sylas" — the packet levelChart, and what whys[6] already says. "Ambessa" is 7 characters against 5 for "Skill" and "Sylas". Level 1 I was able to flip, since Skill and Sylas are both 5.

CHAMPION-LEVEL FABRICATION seen again, four times here: "R passive armor-pen" / "R passive heals you on every hit". Public Execution has neither. Still outstanding across the champion: "Medarda Maxim", a non-existent Ambessa passive, 6 occurrences in champ-data/content/ambessa.js.
